interest: This docket list provides a valuable index and high-level chronology of how U.S. diplomats monitored Japan's acute agrarian crisis during the early 1930s, a pivotal socioeconomic driver of rural unrest, political radicalization, and the rise of Japanese militarism during the Great Depression. It records specific proposed remedies, such as petitions for three-year debt moratoria and government fertilizer subsidies, as well as diplomatic reports from Harbin highlighting external perceptions and fears of agrarian revolution in Japan. Additionally, it illuminates State Department record-keeping practices—showing cross-references to political reports and other decimal files—and captures later technical interest in hydroponic liquid farming.
overview: This file consists of two sheets of the Department of State's List of Papers (docket list) for decimal file 894.61 (Internal Affairs of Japan: Agriculture), indexing documents and cross-references entered between 1930 and the 1940s. The recorded entries (sub-numbers 14 through 22) document the severe economic distress and social unrest affecting Japanese rural farming communities during the Great Depression, petitions submitted by agricultural bodies requesting a three-year moratorium on farmers' debts and government subsidies for fertilizer, and extraordinary sessions of the Imperial Diet convened to address the crisis. In addition, the list records diplomatic reports from Harbin regarding fears of agrarian revolution in Japan, despatches by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew and Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville analyzing agrarian legislation and legal restrictions on foreign exploitation of natural resources, and a submission on hydroponics (liquid farming) by George Danich.

subfiles.about: A Department of State list of papers indexing records, reports, and cross-references filed under decimal file 894.61 concerning Japanese agriculture and agrarian relief between 1930 and 1945.
subfiles.summary: This two-page docket list (Form DS-46) indexes records filed under decimal file 894.61 concerning agriculture in Japan across sub-numbers 14 through 22. It details reports and cross-references regarding the severe agrarian depression and social unrest in Japanese farming communities, petitions for three-year debt moratoria and state fertilizer aid, and extraordinary Diet sessions convened to address the rural plight. It also notes diplomatic communications from Joseph C. Grew and Edwin L. Neville on agrarian legislation and natural resource restrictions, observations from Harbin concerning rumors of agrarian revolution, and an article on hydroponics transmitted by George Danich.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers for File 894.61: Agriculture - Japan
